marketing_wrapper: Warm off-white (#f5f2ed) backdrop with a centred two-line caption in the top ~20%, then a frameless rounded phone screen (no bezel, ~75%) cropped at the bottom so the tab bar never shows. All six frames are real UI: home (All), Homes tab, Paris itinerary map + sheet, Services, an Experience detail, and the friends Travel map.

typography.display: Airbnb Cereal (the brand's custom geometric sans) in semibold for section headers (Recently viewed, Popular experiences in Los Angeles), sheet titles (Paris, Travel map) and listing titles; captions use the same face
typography.numerals: proportional Cereal; prices and ratings inline ($884 for 2 nights · ★4.86); dates as May 15 – 19; day numbers in small grey circles on the itinerary rail
typography.weights: Semibold headers and titles, regular grey metadata; medium in chips
typography.case_and_tracking: Sentence case; tight display tracking in captions; one small all-caps label on the 3D calendar (STARTS IN / DAYS)

palette.accent_strategy: Near-silent: one brand red/pink appears only as tiny moments (heart badges on map pins, the red '7' on the 3D calendar); everything else is black text, grey metadata and photography. Colour comes from photos and the 3D icon objects.
palette.source: palette.json 01–06: #f5f2ed 24–32% = marketing backdrop; #ffffff 20–32% = app background; #e8e6e2 / #e4e3de = chip and card fills; #83786d / #897162 / #8c7761 = photo content. #bae8f7 in 06 = map water. Brand pink is a visual estimate.

shape.radius_language: large and pill: ~20pt listing photo corners, ~20pt cards and sheets, pill search bar and raised category chips, circular arrow buttons and avatars
shape.borders_shadows: Soft, diffuse drop shadows under the search pill, category chips, cards and the sheet (the chips look raised and pressable); no hard borders; hairline divider inside the stay card
shape.materials: Mostly flat white with soft elevation; the selected category chip looks inset/pressed (darker grey with inner shading); 3D rendered objects as icons

liquid_glass_visible: no (raised soft-shadow pills, not translucent glass)
density: medium: horizontally scrolling carousels of ~145pt photo cards with two text lines each; section headers with arrow buttons every ~300pt
layout: Home: pill 'Start your search' at top, horizontal category pills (All / Homes / Experiences / Services) with 3D icons, an upcoming-trip card with a 3D tear-off calendar, then stacked horizontal carousels (Recently viewed, Popular experiences) of rounded photo cards with heart toggles and 'Popular'/'Guest favorite' badges.
navigation: Bottom tab bar not visible (cropped by the marketing frame). Top: floating search pill; category switcher as raised pill chips; detail uses a plain back arrow with share/heart icons; maps use a bottom sheet with grab handle, back circle and a vertical day rail.
imagery_and_icons: Professional photography for listings and experiences; soft, glossy 3D rendered objects as category and service icons (globe, house, hot-air balloon, concierge bell, red car, luggage, grocery bag, door, calendar); custom 3D-ish map pins with heart badges; thin outline UI glyphs (heart, share, arrow).
signature_visual_move: Small glossy 3D objects (hot-air balloon, concierge bell, tear-off calendar) used as icons inside otherwise flat white, photo-led chrome.
tells_present: Cards everywhere (carousel of photo cards per section)

direction_fit.why: The 3D pictograph system is confined to category chips, service tiles, map pins and the trip calendar, with the rest typographic and photo-led, exactly as the 'dimensional variant' description and the open-design.ai split say. The direction rests on a small share of pixels, so the 3D icons are a seasoning over a conventional marketplace layout.

notes: Brand red is far rarer than expected: there are no red CTAs in any frame. The soft raised chips with shadows read as tactile rather than glass. The tab bar can't be judged.
